newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Suspected bombers held near Sri Lanka leader's home.
newsitem.headline: Suspected bombers held near Sri Lanka leader's home.

text.p: A group of 20 suspected suicide bombers have been arrested near Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga's official residence, a police officer said on Wednesday.

The arrests followed police warnings this week that between 25 and 30 suicide bombers of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) sneaked into Colombo on a mission to retaliate against a recent offensive by the military.
"A group of 20 suspected bombers were arrested at Colpetty area yesterday. They are now under interrogation," the officer at Colpetty Police Station told Reuters.
Kumaratunga's official residence, called Temple Trees, is located in the Colpetty area.
"The arrests were made during a six-hour search operation launched on information LTTE suicide bombers had infiltrated the Colpetty area," the officer said.

The LTTE, fighting for a separate state for the Tamil ethnic minority in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka, bombed the central bank in Colombo in January, killing nearly 100 people, and blew up a train in a suburb of the capital in July, killing 57.
Police and the military have been placed on high alert in Colombo since the army began a fresh offensive against the LTTE last month.
The army late last month captured the LTTE's northern stronghold of Kilinochchi, the last major town controlled by the rebels, after eight days of fierce fighting.
The LTTE has frequently bombed government and civilian facilities in retaliation for major army offensives.
The government has said more than 50,000 people have died in the 13-year ethnic war.
